definition: the state of being dormant or delayed until conditions allow activity
memoryTip: Latent stage — hidden or idle until something triggers it.
correctPassage: There is often a latency between infection and the appearance of symptoms.
wrongPassages: The latency of the fireworks display meant the sky lit up the instant the switch was flipped.
She measured the drawer labeled latency and found only pens and spare batteries inside.
His latency attendance meant he never missed a single class all year.

definition: develop slowly under favorable conditions; keep warm to hatch or grow
memoryTip: Like eggs in an incubator — grow slowly under steady care.
correctPassage: The startup will incubate new ideas before seeking outside investment.
wrongPassages: They hoped to incubate the scandal by leaking it to every outlet at once.
She incubated the walkout by locking the doors and cutting badge access mid-meeting.
He tried to incubate the rumor by demanding an immediate public retraction.

definition: combined effect greater than the sum of the parts
memoryTip: Syn + energy: working together multiplies the power.
correctPassage: The merger was sold on the promise of synergy between the two product lines.
wrongPassages: Working alone, she produced more synergy than the entire committee combined.
The rivalry created synergy by ensuring the two teams never shared data.
Each department claimed synergy while refusing every joint project on the calendar.

definition: wary and careful; unwilling to take unnecessary risks
memoryTip: Circum-spect: look all around before you step.
correctPassage: Lawyers advised a circumspect response until more facts were known.
wrongPassages: His circumspect dive off the pier ignored every posted warning about the rocks.
A circumspect investor poured the entire savings account into a single unvetted tip.
She gave a circumspect answer that named names and promised results by Friday.

memoryTip: Without guile (tricks) — open, honest, nothing up the sleeve.
correctPassage: His guileless manner made colleagues trust him quickly.
wrongPassages: The guileless con artist ran three aliases and a fake charity for years.
Her guileless contract buried the fees in footnotes no customer would read.
A guileless witness changed the story three times and denied knowing the defendant.

definition: pacify someone by giving in to demands
memoryTip: A-peace: buy quiet by yielding a little (or a lot).
correctPassage: Concessions intended to appease critics only encouraged further demands.
wrongPassages: Leaders chose to appease the protest by refusing every demand on the list.
She tried to appease the customer by hanging up before he finished speaking.
They tried to appease the deadline by ignoring it until after the due date had passed.

definition: teach someone to accept a set of beliefs uncritically
memoryTip: In-doctrine: pour in a doctrine; no free questioning allowed.
correctPassage: The camp was accused of trying to indoctrinate children rather than educate them.
wrongPassages: Good seminars indoctrinate students by inviting them to challenge every claim.
She hoped to indoctrinate the class with open debate and competing sources.
The lab manual was designed to indoctrinate curiosity, not a single fixed theory.

definition: new and experimental, especially in the arts
memoryTip: French for "vanguard" — out front of the artistic pack.
correctPassage: The gallery specializes in avant-garde work that challenges traditional form.
wrongPassages: The avant-garde tax table simply restated last year's ordinary rates with no changes.
Engineers measured the avant-garde of the bridge as 214.6 meters of standard steel.
An avant-garde crowd of two was listed as a sold-out premiere in the press release.

definition: intellectual rather than emotional or physical
memoryTip: Cerebrum = brain — more thinking than feeling.
correctPassage: The film is more cerebral than emotional, built around ideas rather than action.
wrongPassages: The cerebral chase scene was pure spectacle, with almost no dialogue or theme.
Fans loved the cerebral finale for its tears, hugs, and zero discussion of ideas.
Coaches designed a cerebral drill that tested only sprint speed and vertical jump.

definition: persuade by flattery or gentle urging
memoryTip: Cage + jolly talk — sweet-talk someone into the cage (or the favor).
correctPassage: She tried to cajole reluctant volunteers into staffing the event.
wrongPassages: He tried to cajole the guard by shouting threats and slamming the counter.
They cajoled the board with a silent spreadsheet and no conversation at all.
Voters buried the cajole bond that engineers had labeled urgent and overdue.
